# casdoor_rule (Resource)

Manages a Casdoor rule, a web application firewall rule applied by sites.

Only the attributes set in the configuration are written to Casdoor. The other fields of the object, including the ones not listed here, keep their current values.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "casdoor_rule" "block_bots" {
  owner  = casdoor_organization.acme.name
  name   = "block-bots"
  type   = "User-Agent"
  action = "Block"
  reason = "Your request is blocked."

  expressions = [
    {
      name     = "bots"
      operator = "contains"
      value    = "BadBot"
    },
  ]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) The name of the rule, unique within its owner.
- `owner` (String) The organization that the object belongs to.

### Optional

- `action` (String) What happens to a matching request, e.g. `Block`.
- `expressions` (Attributes List) The expressions that a request is matched against. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--expressions))
- `is_verbose` (Boolean) Whether the response explains which rule matched.
- `reason` (String) The message returned to a blocked request.
- `status_code` (Number) The HTTP status code returned to a blocked request.
- `type` (String) The type of the rule, e.g. `User-Agent`.

### Read-Only

- `created_time` (String) The time when the rule was created.
- `id` (String) The ID of the rule in the `owner/name` format.

<a id="nestedatt--expressions"></a>
### Nested Schema for `expressions`

Required:

- `name` (String) The name of the expression.

Optional:

- `operator` (String) The operator.
- `value` (String) The value.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import with the organization and the name.
terraform import casdoor_rule.example <organization>/<name>
```
